signals.entity: National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia (NBRM) / Bank of Italy TIPS Clone
signals.signal: Second wave of the Western Balkans TIPS Clone instant-payment platform: North Macedonia, Albania and Kosovo are due to join in November 2026, after Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro went live on 20/07/2026. The platform is a clone of the Eurosystem TARGET Instant Payment Settlement service, operated with the Bank of Italy and ECB support, settling in central-bank money in local currency and euro.
signals.implies: Three more Printec markets get a 24/7 instant rail in one quarter. Every participating bank needs ISO 20022 message handling, real-time posting, alias/proxy lookup and — critically — REAL-TIME fraud screening, which legacy batch AML tools cannot do. Direct pull for Printec transaction monitoring/fraud, AML/compliance and payments integration; secondary pull on ATM/POS channels that must expose the new rail.
signals.likelihood: High that go-live lands in Nov-2026/Q1-2027; bank-side readiness projects run now
signals.followup: Get the NBRM, Bank of Albania and BQK official participation notices and the per-bank onboarding waves; map which of the ~13 MK / ~11 AL / ~11 XK banks lack a real-time fraud engine.

signals.signal: North Macedonia will run TWO parallel instant-payment infrastructures: KIBS holds an instant-payment system operator licence and runs 'KIBS Instant' plus the 'Strela' mobile app (account-to-account, QR, NFC contactless, in-store and e-commerce payments, alias register, request-to-pay), with two banks preparing to join by 15/09/2026 — alongside the NBRM's TIPS Clone from November 2026.
signals.implies: A dual-rail market forces every MK bank to integrate twice and to reconcile across two schemes. Printec's payments integration, POS/QR acceptance and transaction-monitoring lines all get pulled in; the QR/NFC overlay is a direct softPOS/POS opportunity at merchant level.
signals.likelihood: Near-certain — first two banks named for 15/09/2026
signals.followup: Identify the two banks joining KIBS Instant by 15/09/2026 and confirm from KIBS's own site; check whether NBRM will mandate interoperability between KIBS Instant and TIPS Clone.

signals.signal: PROGRAM: a four-role cluster advertised simultaneously for a single NEW branch in Deçan — 'Menaxher i Degës (Deçan)' (Branch Manager), 'Menaxher i Marrëdhënieve për klientë Individual (Deçan)', 'Menaxher për Marrëdhënie me NVM (Deçan)' (SME relationship manager) and 'Zyrtar i ri Operacioneve Bankare (Deçan)' (new banking-operations officer), all posted around 18/08/2026 on KosovaJob.
signals.implies: Four roles for one location is a branch OPENING, not attrition backfill — Kosovo's best-rated bank is expanding its physical network westward. A new branch needs an ATM/recycler, teller cash automation, queue/self-service and card-issuance capability: a clean Printec self-service + cash-automation entry point.
signals.likelihood: High — branch opening implied within 3-6 months
signals.followup: Confirm the Deçan branch opening from TEB's own site/BQK branch register; ask whether more locations follow; identify TEB Kosovo's incumbent ATM vendor.

signals.signal: Two technology vacancies posted in August 2026 on Zaposli.me: 'Vođa tima za upravljanje podacima i vještačkom inteligencijom' (Team Lead, Data Management and Artificial Intelligence), Podgorica, posted 24/08/2026; and 'Senior Developer Specialist (M/Ž/D) – Sektor IT&Organizacije', Kotor/Podgorica, posted 12/08/2026. These are the ONLY two bank vacancies in the whole Bankarstvo category (6 ads total across all employers).
signals.implies: Erste Montenegro is building an in-house data/AI capability rather than buying it — a signal of a data-platform programme. Adjacent Printec pull: AML/transaction-monitoring analytics and fraud scoring feed off exactly this data layer, and the bank now has an internal owner to sell to.
signals.likelihood: Medium — roles live, programme scope unstated
signals.followup: Find the Erste Montenegro data/AI programme scope; check whether the AI team lead role maps to Erste Group's regional data platform or a local build.

signals.entity: Montenegrin banking sector (Hipotekarna banka, CKB/OTP, NLB Banka Podgorica, Addiko ME, Lovćen, Universal Capital, Prva, Ziraat ME, Adriatic, ESOP, Komercijalna)
signals.signal: ZERO-POSTING FINDING: on 31/08/2026 the Bankarstvo (banking) category on Zaposli.me — Montenegro's main job board — held only 6 ads in total, of which only two were from a bank (both Erste). No ATM, self-service, cash-management, payments-product, card/acquiring or branch-network role from ANY Montenegrin bank. The Hipotekarna banka 'ATM specijalista' vacancy first seen 17/06/2026 has still NOT been re-posted.
signals.implies: Six weeks after Montenegro's TIPS-Clone instant-payment go-live (20/07/2026) there is NO visible hiring build-out. Either the banks resourced it inside existing teams, or they are buying capability from vendors — the second reading is the Printec opening. Treat Montenegro as a vendor-led, not hire-led, market.
signals.likelihood: High that capability is bought rather than hired
signals.followup: Check each Montenegrin bank's own /karijera page directly (zaposli.me is not exhaustive) and the CBCG public register; approach CKB and Hipotekarna on managed services for the instant rail.

signals.signal: Nine live vacancies on the bank's own Oglasi page on 31/08/2026, including 'Saradnik za prihvat kartica' (Card Acceptance / merchant-acquiring associate) — NEW versus the 22/07/2026 baseline — alongside 'Voditelj odjeljenja informacione sigurnosti i IKT rizika' (Head of Information Security and ICT Risk, STILL LIVE from 22/07), 'Direktor Sektora finansijskog upravljanja', two Vogošća branch roles including a 'Blagajnik' (teller) and a data-protection specialist.
signals.source_name: ZiraatBank BH d.d. — Oglasi (own careers page)
signals.implies: A card-acceptance hire plus a still-unfilled InfoSec/ICT-risk head is the signature of a bank standing up merchant acquiring while its security function is under-resourced. Direct fit for Printec POS/acquiring and for HSM/security plus managed services; the Vogošća teller role signals a branch being staffed, i.e. cash-automation demand.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High — acquiring build already staffed for
signals.followup: Download the 'Saradnik za prihvat kartica' .doc to get the application deadline and the reporting line; establish whether ZiraatBank BH acquires directly or through BAMCARD/Monri.

signals.signal: The bank publishes a customer notice titled 'Nova funkcionalnost – Cash IN na bankomatima' (new functionality: cash-IN at ATMs), i.e. it has enabled cash DEPOSIT at its ATM fleet rather than withdrawal only.
signals.implies: Cash-in at the ATM means deposit-capable or recycling machines are already in the estate. Confirms a live recycler refresh cycle in BiH and an entry point for Printec cash-automation, recycler retrofit, cash-cycle managed services and CIT-cost optimisation.
signals.followup: Get the notice's publication date and the number/locations of cash-in ATMs; identify the hardware vendor behind the deposit modules.

signals.signal: LEADERSHIP: Hrisula Kutudi received a new FOUR-YEAR mandate as head of Stopanska banka AD Skopje (announced 18/08/2026), and on the same day the bank expanded its Supervisory Board with Zorica Božinovska-Lazarevska as a new INDEPENDENT member (UKIM accounting/audit professor), following a shareholder-assembly decision approved by the National Bank's Executive Board.
signals.implies: Leadership continuity at North Macedonia's largest bank plus a strengthened board means the existing strategy — including the branch-modernisation programme (the 'Sobranie' digital-concept branch, 13/07/2026) and the vault/cash-management hiring seen in July — carries forward rather than being frozen by a transition. A four-year mandate is the moment to pitch multi-year managed services and a self-service refresh.
signals.followup: Confirm from Stopanska banka's own investor page and the MSE/SEI-Net disclosure; map the branch-modernisation roll-out plan beyond the Sobranie branch.

signals.signal: 'NLB Smart POS' launched/promoted for small businesses — a softPOS-style acceptance product presented by Kristina Trpezanovska as giving small merchants easier access to digital payments. Separately, on 13/07/2026 NLB Banka modernised its 'Sobranie' branch into a digital-concept branch.
signals.implies: softPOS ('tap-to-phone') displaces classic terminals at the micro-merchant end but expands the acquiring estate overall — it needs merchant onboarding/eKYC, terminal management, key injection and HSM-backed security. Direct pull on Printec POS/acquiring, digital onboarding and HSM/security; the digital branch is a self-service/branch-transformation reference point.
signals.followup: Confirm from NLB Banka Skopje's own site who supplies the Smart POS platform (NLB Group-wide vs local); get merchant numbers.

signals.signal: 'Cashless Bitola' initiative — a bank-led programme to digitalise local businesses in Bitola with merchant-acceptance incentives, launched 21/07/2026 and extended with new business benefits announced 18/08/2026.
signals.implies: A city-scale merchant-acceptance push means a burst of new POS/softPOS terminal deployments and merchant onboarding in a single geography — the cleanest kind of POS estate expansion to quantify and quote for. Ties to Printec POS/acquiring and digital onboarding/eKYC for merchant KYC.
signals.followup: Get terminal counts and whether Halkbank MK is extending 'Cashless' to other cities; identify its current POS supplier.

signals.signal: Online consumer loans of up to MKD 2.6 million are now originated end-to-end through 'OneID' — the national digital-identity scheme — i.e. fully remote onboarding and signing with no branch visit.
signals.implies: National eID-based remote origination is now live at MK's second-largest bank at material ticket sizes. That sets the competitive floor: peer banks must match it, which is exactly a digital onboarding/eKYC plus AML-screening sale for Printec across the other MK banks that have not yet integrated OneID.
signals.likelihood: High — live product; peers must follow
signals.followup: Confirm on kb.com.mk; establish which MK banks are NOT yet on OneID — those are the targets.

signals.signal: LEADERSHIP: change in the Supervisory Board with a new member appointed (announced 21/08/2026); separately Maja Mihajlova was RE-appointed to the Management Board (14/08/2026).
signals.implies: Governance refresh at a bank whose model is explicitly electronic-channel-first ('clients who prefer to bank through electronic channels'). Board renewal is the window for a channel/self-service refresh conversation; ProCredit's near-branchless model runs on 24/7 self-service zones, which is core Printec ATM/recycler territory.
signals.followup: Name the new Supervisory Board member from the NBRM approval notice; check ProCredit MK's 24/7 zone estate size.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina (CBBiH) — IPS BiH
signals.signal: The IPS BiH instant-payment participant list on the CBBiH's own page now shows FIVE banks — Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, Raiffeisen Bank BiH, Sparkasse Bank BiH plus NOVA BANKA and ATOS BANK — up from the THREE that went live at launch on 20/07/2026. The CBBiH states the system is open to all commercial banks from day one and that the rest join as they complete technical adaptation. The three launch banks together held about a quarter of BiH banking-sector assets.
signals.source_name: Centralna banka Bosne i Hercegovine — Instant platni sistemi (IPS BiH)
signals.implies: Two more banks joined inside six weeks and roughly fifteen more BiH banks are still outside the scheme — a named, finite, dated pipeline of integration projects. Each joiner needs ISO 20022 messaging, 24/7 real-time posting and real-time fraud screening. This is the single clearest Printec pipeline in BiH: payments integration, transaction monitoring/fraud, and managed services for banks too small to run 24/7 operations in-house.
signals.followup: Snapshot the CBBiH participant list monthly to time each approach; target the ~15 non-participants (ASA Banka, ZiraatBank BH, Union banka, BBI, ProCredit BiH, MF banka, NLB banka BL/Sarajevo, Addiko x2, UniCredit BiH x2, Privredna banka Sarajevo, Naša banka, Komercijalno-investiciona banka) with a joiner package.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank International / Addiko Bank AG / Alta Group d.o.o. (Serbia)
signals.signal: CARVE-OUT CONFIRMED AS THE PLAN OF RECORD: RBI will sell Addiko's Serbian, Sarajevo, Banja Luka and Podgorica operations to Alta Group d.o.o. (Serbia), keeping only Croatia, Slovenia and Austria. Addiko CEO Herbert Juranek said on 13/08/2026 that transfer of ownership to RBI should conclude by the end of Q1-2027 at the earliest (offer documents name a 14/05/2027 long-stop), that RBI secured about 55-56% of shares, and that full integration will run 'at least until the end of 2027, probably into 2028'. The EU-unit merger cannot start until the carve-out clears regulators. RBI's own 08/04/2026 offer release confirms the Alta Group carve-out at fair market value; tender completion expected Q4-2026, carve-out closing H2-2027.
signals.source_name: Nachrichten.at (OÖN) interview with Addiko CEO Herbert Juranek; RBI press release 08/04/2026
signals.implies: Addiko BiH (Sarajevo and Banja Luka) and Addiko Montenegro are NOT going into the Raiffeisen estate — they go to Alta Group, a Serbian buyer that is also expanding in North Macedonia. That means a full re-platforming and re-branding of three Western Balkan banks under a new owner in 2027-2028: card re-issuance, ATM/POS re-branding and re-certification, new core/channel integration, fresh AML/transaction-monitoring stack. A rare, dated, multi-country integration window for Printec self-service, POS/acquiring, AML and managed services — and it is a competitive land-grab because the incumbent vendors are Addiko-group contracts that will be re-tendered.
signals.likelihood: High that the carve-out proceeds; timing risk on regulatory approval
signals.followup: Track the ECB/competition approvals and the Alta Group transaction agreement; identify Alta Group's existing vendor stack in Serbia and North Macedonia (ALTA Banka AD Skopje) — that stack is the default winner unless displaced early.

signals.entity: Bank of Albania (Banka e Shqipërisë) — Governor Gent Sejko
signals.signal: Governor Gent Sejko confirmed at the 05/08/2026 monetary-policy press briefing that Albania will complete integration into the TIPS Clone instant-payment system in NOVEMBER 2026 at the latest, built with the Bank of Italy, the ECB and the Albanian banking system. The Bank of Albania estimates the financial system could save up to ALL 35 billion a year from a shift to electronic payments; if only half of transactions migrate, businesses save about ALL 1 billion and individuals about ALL 500 million a year.
signals.source_name: Albeu.com reporting Bank of Albania Governor's press briefing
signals.implies: A governor-level, dated November commitment means every Albanian bank has a hard Q4-2026 integration deadline running right now. Combined with Albania's earlier SEPA entry, this is a compressed payments-modernisation window: ISO 20022 handling, 24/7 availability, real-time fraud screening and reconciliation. Direct Printec pull on payments integration, transaction monitoring/AML and managed services.
signals.likelihood: High — governor-level commitment with a named month
signals.followup: Get the Bank of Albania's own njoftim/press release and the participant-bank list; identify which of Albania's 11 banks have not contracted a real-time fraud engine.

signals.signal: Six weeks after go-live, CBCG reports instant-payment volume grew roughly FIVE-FOLD from about 2,500 transactions on launch day (20/07/2026) to five times that by end-July, with 56,678 transactions in the first 12 days. All 11 Montenegrin banks joined simultaneously, making Montenegro the first Western Balkan country with sector-wide instant payments. The fee is capped at five cents for electronic transfers up to EUR 200. CBCG director Valentina Bulatović notes payments now register at midnight hours. Electronic transactions are currently 60% of credit transfers.
signals.source_name: Adria TV / portalanalitika.me reporting Central Bank of Montenegro
signals.implies: A five-cent price cap on sub-EUR-200 transfers destroys the economics of manual exception handling and of any batch fraud process — banks must automate or lose money per transaction. Round-the-clock volume also removes the overnight maintenance window, which is exactly the argument for Printec managed services plus real-time transaction monitoring. Rising account-to-account volume also pressures the ATM cash cycle: fewer, better-utilised machines, i.e. a recycler business case.
signals.followup: Get the CBCG's own statistical release with the August figures and the split by bank; check whether ATM withdrawal volumes fell in Q3-2026.

signals.signal: ZERO/LOW-POSTING FINDING: on 31/08/2026 duapune.com — Albania's largest job portal — held 845 active postings nationwide, of which only 6 were 'Arkëtar Banke' (bank teller). Across the whole Finance and IT taxonomy there was NO ATM, self-service, cash-management, card/acquiring, POS, payments-product, digital-channels or AML/financial-crime role at any Albanian bank. Bank career portals are largely closed to plain fetch: tiranabank.zohorecruit.eu is fully JS-hydrated and yields 0 enumerable roles, and bkt.com.al, raiffeisen.al and bankacredins.com career paths 404 or fail.
signals.implies: Albania faces a November TIPS deadline with no visible payments hiring. That is the strongest possible buy-not-build signal in the market: the capability is being bought from vendors and integrators in Q3-2026, right now. Printec should approach Albanian banks on outsourced instant-payment integration, fraud screening and managed services rather than waiting for postings that will never appear.
signals.followup: Escalate the Albanian bank career portals to a browser session (Claude-in-Chrome) to enumerate the JS-hydrated boards; check LinkedIn Albania for bank payments roles.

signals.signal: ABI Bank's own site presents its self-service network under a dedicated 'ATM Euronet' menu item alongside 'Degë dhe ATM' — i.e. its customer-facing ATM access is provided through the Euronet network rather than a wholly self-operated fleet.
signals.source_name: ABI Bank (American Bank of Investments) — official website navigation
signals.implies: COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE: Euronet — an ATM-as-a-service operator, not a hardware vendor — already holds the self-service relationship at a mid-sized Albanian bank. Euronet has taken the same position at CrediaBank in Greece. This is the outsourcing model Printec must beat or match with its own managed-services proposition across the Western Balkans.
signals.followup: Establish the commercial form of the ABI/Euronet arrangement (branding, ownership of machines, term); map how many other AL/XK/MK banks have outsourced ATMs to Euronet.

signals.signal: [STANDING, dated 03/10/2025 — re-verify] The Bank of Albania plans to cap interchange at EU levels of 0.2% (debit) and 0.3% (credit), which it expects to cut total merchant service charges from about 2-2.5% to around 1%. Albania had 27,969 POS terminals at mid-2025, up 28.4% year on year; in H1-2025 there were 12.57 million card transactions at POS worth ALL 48.3 billion, +42% year on year, with card payments already exceeding ATM cash withdrawals by count.
signals.source_name: Monitor.al reporting Bank of Albania Deputy Director of Payments Valentina Semi
signals.implies: A ~28% annual growth rate in the POS estate is the fastest terminal expansion in Printec's small-market footprint, and an interchange cap accelerates it further by making acceptance cheap for merchants. Straight POS/acquiring and merchant-onboarding/eKYC opportunity; the cap also squeezes acquirer margins, which favours low-cost softPOS and outsourced terminal estate management.
signals.likelihood: Medium — regulation announced, adoption date not confirmed
signals.followup: CRITICAL RE-VERIFY: has the interchange regulation been adopted since Oct-2025? Pull the Bank of Albania's H1-2026 payment statistics for the current POS count and the ATM/POS crossover trend.

signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (BQK/CBK) / Kosovo banking sector
signals.signal: CBK data show the Kosovo banking sector earned EUR 113.8 million net profit in the first seven months of 2026, up from EUR 103.9 million in the same period of 2025 — a rise of EUR 9.9 million or +9.5%.
signals.source_name: Bankarstvo.mk reporting Central Bank of Kosovo (BQK) data
signals.implies: Rising sector profitability is capex headroom, and it lands in the same quarter as Kosovo's November TIPS Clone entry and TEB's branch expansion. Kosovo's banks can fund self-service refresh, POS estate growth and a fraud/AML platform now rather than deferring — the budget argument that usually blocks small-market deals is weak this cycle.
signals.followup: Pull the figures from the BQK's own monthly statistical bulletin (site currently 403 to scripted fetch) and add ATM/POS/card counts from the BQK payment statistics.

signals.entity: Kosovo Banking Association (KBA) + Visa + Helvetas / Sweden-Sverige / IMAA
signals.signal: 'Paguaj me një TAP' / 'Pay with One TAP' — a coordinated Tap-to-Phone (softPOS) rollout programme for Kosovo merchants, run by the Kosovo Banking Association with Visa and donor partners. Merchant information events ran in Prishtina (16/04/2026), Prizren (25/05/2026 and earlier), and Gjakovë (10/06/2026 and 25/06/2026). The KBA describes it as 'transforming the way payments are made in Kosovo'.
signals.source_name: Kosovo Banking Association — News and Activity Schedule
signals.implies: An association-level, donor-funded softPOS push means merchant acceptance in Kosovo will expand fast and cheaply on phones rather than terminals. For Printec this cuts both ways: it compresses classic POS hardware demand but creates demand for the acquiring back end — merchant onboarding/eKYC, terminal/device management, key injection and HSM-backed security — which softPOS still requires. Sell the platform, not the box.
signals.likelihood: High — programme actively running with events
signals.followup: Identify which Kosovo banks acquire for the Tap-to-Phone scheme and whose softPOS platform is behind it; get merchant enrolment numbers from the KBA.

signals.entity: Agjencia e Regjistrimit Civil (ARC) + Kosovo Banking Association member banks
signals.signal: The Civil Registration Agency, supported by the Kosovo Banking Association, finalised a NEW DRAFT REGULATION allowing banks to update customer data WITHOUT the customer being physically present — i.e. remote identity verification against the national civil register.
signals.implies: A legal route to remote KYC refresh against the state register is the precondition for digital onboarding at scale. Every Kosovo bank will need an eKYC/identity-verification integration to the ARC register plus the AML screening that goes with it. This is a direct, regulation-driven Printec digital onboarding/eKYC and AML/compliance opportunity across all Kosovo banks at once.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High — draft finalised, adoption status to confirm
signals.followup: Confirm whether the regulation has been ADOPTED and published in the Official Gazette since May 2026, and get its compliance date — that date is the sales trigger.

signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (CBK) + Kosovo Banking Association
signals.signal: CBK and the KBA held a joint workshop on advancing Kosovo's instant-payment infrastructure. The CBK Deputy Governor framed accelerated digitalisation and innovative payment solutions as a key priority on the CBK's institutional agenda, and the Director of the CBK Payments Department presented work in progress on the 'TIPS Clone' platform and SEPA integration. Kosovo is in the November 2026 TIPS Clone second wave alongside Albania and North Macedonia.
signals.source_name: Kosovo Banking Association — 'Kosovo banking sector moves towards instant payments'
signals.implies: Kosovo's banks are being brought to the instant rail collectively, through the association, rather than one at a time — which means a single association-level or CBK-level engagement can reach the whole sector. Printec should pitch a shared instant-payment readiness and real-time fraud-screening package via the KBA rather than bank by bank.
signals.followup: Get the CBK's own TIPS Clone project page and participation notice (bqk-kos.org is 403 to scripted fetch — escalate to a browser session); obtain the KBA Payments Committee membership.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed for 2026-08-31). Covered all five markets. PRIMARY sources opened: CBBiH IPS BiH participant page (regulator), ZiraatBank BH Oglasi (bank's own page), Zaposli.me Bankarstvo category (ME), KosovaJob TEB Banka employer page and the Deçan branch-manager posting (XK), duapune.com category taxonomy (AL), bankarstvo.mk WordPress REST API (MK — the productive route: /wp-json/wp/v2/posts with search and after parameters), Kosovo Banking Association news page, ABI Bank site (AL), RBI press release, Bank of Albania site. WHAT CHANGED vs the 31/07 baseline: (1) the Western Balkans TIPS Clone SECOND WAVE — AL, XK, MK in November 2026 — was not in the baseline at all and is the largest new signal; (2) IPS BiH participants grew 3 -> 5 (Nova Banka, Atos Bank added) since the 20/07 launch; (3) the RBI/Addiko outcome is now materially more specific — the BiH and Montenegro units are being CARVED OUT to Alta Group (Serbia), not integrated into RBI, with a Q1-2027 ownership transfer and integration into 2027-2028; (4) North Macedonia will run TWO instant rails (KIBS Instant + Strela app, first two banks by 15/09/2026, plus NBRM TIPS Clone); (5) new MK leadership: Hrisula Kutudi re-mandated at Stopanska banka and a new independent Supervisory Board member (both 18/08), ProCredit MK board changes (14/08 and 21/08). STATUSED baseline items: ALTA Banka AD Skopje's three July postings and Stopanska banka's 'Трезорист' vault role can no longer be confirmed — no MK bank publishes an enumerable board (recorded as a finding); Hipotekarna banka's 'ATM specijalista' (17/06) has STILL not been re-posted; ZiraatBank BH's InfoSec/ICT-risk head role from 22/07 is STILL LIVE and a NEW card-acceptance role has appeared alongside it.
